name: Yellow/red air-threat-level reform: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 1092 of 4 Sep 2026 ('Certain issues of optimizing population protection and responding to threats of air attack means'), amended by No. 1128 of 15 Sep 2026; announced via ArmyInform and Euromaidan Press
type: document (primary legal act + official/semi-official news coverage); defines the regime change, not a model
url: Resolution text/metadata: https://zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/1092-2026-п (body returned 403 to scripts on 2026-10-17; metadata only) ; ArmyInform 2 Sep announcement: https://armyinform.com.ua/2026/09/02/zhovtyj-i-chervonyj-rivni-v-ukrayini-zminyat-systemu-opovishhennya-pro-povitryani-zagrozy/ ; ArmyInform 4 Sep 'Two levels introduced': https://armyinform.com.ua/2026/09/04/dva-rivni-povitryanyh-tryvog-zaprovadyly-v-ukrayini-yak-cze-praczyuvatyme/ (EN: https://armyinform.com.ua/en/2026/09/08/two-levels-of-air-raid-alerts-introduced-in-ukraine-how-will-they-work/) ; Euromaidan Press 4 Sep: https://euromaidanpress.com/?p=424042 ; Kyiv launch (UNN): https://unn.ua/en/amp/a-differentiated-color-coded-threat-alert-system-has-been-launched-in-kyiv ; Mykolaiv pilot: https://korabelov.info/en/?p=613036 ; MVS explanation via Ministry of Economy: https://me.gov.ua/Documents/Detail/9d4bebb9-1580-4d6e-98a4-edfac4ea3f47?lang=uk-UA ; No.1128 coverage: https://news.dtkt.ua/society/economics/114792-z-18-veresnia-diiut-onovleni-pravila-roboti-biznesu-ta-biudzetnix-ustanov-pid-cas-trivog-postanova-kmu-1128
year: 2026. Announced by President Zelensky 2 Sep 2026; Cabinet decision announced 3 Sep; Resolution No. 1092 dated 4 Sep 2026 per zakon.rada.gov.ua (some outlets say 3 Sep), published in Uriadovyi Kurier 4 Sep; Kyiv differentiated alerts from 6 Sep 2026 06:00 local; Mykolaiv oblast pilot reported 8 Sep; amendment No. 1128 of 15 Sep 2026 in force from 18 Sep 2026 (current Rada version dated 18.09.2026); MVS explanations 5 Oct and updated 14 Oct 2026. Checked 2026-10-17.
authors: Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (PM Serhii Koretskyi announced); President Volodymyr Zelensky (initial announcement); ArmyInform (Ministry of Defence news agency, no byline on the 4/8 Sep piece); Euromaidan Press article by Zoriana Katola; Ministry of Internal Affairs (explanatory notes published on me.gov.ua by the Ministry of Economy's security-and-defence economic policy department).
popularity: Not applicable (legal act and news). Widely covered by Ukrainian media (Mind, TSN, DOU, Ligazakon, Debet-Kredit, Kadroland, Interfax-Ukraine, Ukranews).
peer_review_status: Primary legal document (official act) plus official/state-media news; not peer-reviewed. The operational criteria behind each level are NOT published: they are set weekly by the military.
target_type: Not applicable (regime definition). Relevance: splits the single 'air alert' STATE into two levels (yellow = drone threat; red = missile / combined / massive drone threat). For our onset target this changes what an 'onset' is: yellow and red become separate signals, a red can start during a yellow, and the any-level onset rate is a different quantity from pre-reform onsets.
target_definition: Not applicable. Level definitions as reported: YELLOW = threat of attack by strike drones; RED = elevated threat of missile (incl. ballistic) or combined missile-and-drone strike, and also massive drone attacks (Kyiv: red covers 'massive drone threat', 'missile threat', 'missile-and-drone threat'). The concrete threat indicators that map to each level are set WEEKLY by the General Staff and Air Force together with the Cabinet, MoD, MVS and DSNS (State Emergency Service) and are not public. All-clear is given when none of the listed threats is recorded.
spatial_unit: Not fixed in the reports reviewed. The act and announcements task officials to develop geographic differentiation so alerts cover only threatened areas (even parts of a city/district); Kyiv rollout was per city district with gaps (Pecherskyi not connected; Holosiivskyi and Sviatoshynskyi partly). In alerts.in.ua data the levels appear on oblast/raion/hromada/city records. [uncertain] exact declaration granularity under No. 1092.
at_risk_masking: Not applicable. Implication: the mask must follow the target level (any-level mask for any-level onset; red-only mask for red onset, where red starting during a yellow counts as an onset) as in CLAUDE.md D-015 / architecture item 4.
data_sources: Primary act: CabMin Resolution No. 1092 (4 Sep 2026), amended by No. 1128 (15 Sep 2026, in force 18 Sep); related No. 1129 (15 Sep 2026, railway operations by threat level). News: ArmyInform (2, 4, 7, 8, 18 Sep 2026), Euromaidan Press (4 Sep 2026), UNN (Kyiv launch 6 Sep), korabelov.info (Mykolaiv pilot 8 Sep), Dengi.ua, Mind.ua, Debet-Kredit. A unified air-threat service in Diia is reported to start 1 Dec 2026 [uncertain].
data_source_variant: Regime-change document. Direct consequence for data: the official Vadimkin/official_data_en.csv froze at 2026-09-07 05:28 UTC, i.e. right after the Kyiv launch (6 Sep) and during the nationwide rollout; post-reform data exist only via alerts.in.ua with alert_level red/yellow (history from 2026-09-12 17:16 UTC in our dump). Rollout was staggered: Kyiv 6 Sep, Mykolaiv pilot ~8 Sep, nationwide differentiation reported from ~8 Sep [uncertain], so early-September level labels may be inconsistent across oblasts.
preprocessing: Not applicable. Implied: treat 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-12 as missing in both sources; do not concatenate pre- and post-reform series; represent alert_level explicitly; level transitions (yellow->red, red->yellow) inside one episode must be handled by the target-level setting, not by merging.
known_label_artefacts: (1) Criteria are set WEEKLY and not published, so the yellow/red labelling rule itself drifts week to week: the new regime is non-stationary by design (D-015 note). (2) Staggered, pilot-mode rollout (Kyiv 6 Sep with district coverage gaps; Mykolaiv 'pilot mode' 8 Sep), so cross-oblast comparability of levels in the first weeks is weak. (3) Repeated all-clear siren cancelled (siren only at alert start) and level-specific sounds planned later: changes the public signal, not necessarily the data feed. (4) Geographic narrowing of alerts is a stated goal; if implemented, per-oblast union intervals will shrink in share of time, independent of threat. (5) Behavioural/economic incentive: yellow lets business operate, red stops it, so there is pressure on how often red is declared. (6) Amendment No. 1128 (18 Sep) changed business/signal-duration rules mid-sample. None of these were 'handled' by the source; they are caveats for our exploratory section.
features: Not applicable. Implication: pre-reform features (onsets_last_24h/7d, minutes_since_last_start, neighbours active) are computed on a single-level signal; after the reform their meaning changes (yellow onsets are more frequent and longer drone raids), so a frozen model sees a shifted feature distribution.
external_feature_timing: Not applicable. Note: the weekly criteria are not published, so they cannot be used as a feature or covariate; any 'regime week' indicator would be unobserved.
split_scheme: Not applicable. Implication: the reform date is a hard structural break; the official-data test (2026-07-27 to 2026-09-07) ends at the break, and any post-reform scoring is a transfer test, not part of the same split.
metrics: Not applicable. Implication: report calibration-in-the-large and within-oblast AUC separately for the new regime, since base rates change by construction.
baseline_strength: Not applicable. Implication: the rolling 14-day recent-rate baseline adapts to the post-reform base rate within two weeks, while a frozen model does not, so recent-rate is expected to be relatively stronger after the reform.
calibration_under_drift: Highly relevant: the reform changes the definition and count of alerts (yellow drone alerts, red missile/massive alerts, geographic narrowing), so a calibration-in-the-large shift is expected a priori, and weekly criteria changes make it non-stationary even within the new regime. One unverified media report claims yellow about 61% and red about 39% of alert time in September 2026 [uncertain] (could not be traced to a primary source).
uncertainty_of_gain: Not applicable. Implication: post-reform window is short (2026-09-13 to 2026-10-12) and its labelling rule shifts weekly, so any measured gain/loss should be treated as exploratory with wide uncertainty.
regime_coverage: This document DEFINES the Sep-2026 yellow/red shift: decision 3-4 Sep 2026, Kyiv live 6 Sep, oblast pilots ~8 Sep, amendment 18 Sep. Our official data end 2026-09-07 05:28 UTC, so they contain at most ~1 day of partial post-reform Kyiv data.
leakage_handling: Not applicable (document). Implication for us: do not use post-reform API data to choose features, thresholds or calibration of the headline model (no tuning on API data, D-015); do not use 'final' level labels revised after the fact; red-only target must use red-active mask built causally from data known at t.
test_window_hygiene: Not applicable. Implication: the new-regime section must be labelled exploratory and kept out of the headline (D-015); the official test window ends before the nationwide rollout, which keeps the headline test within one regime.
headline_results: No model results (legal act). Key facts: two levels introduced by Resolution No. 1092 (4 Sep 2026); yellow = drone threat, businesses with shelter access may operate; red = missile/combined/massive threat, work stops and people go to shelters; businesses without shelters got 3 months (Ministry of Economy deadline 4 Dec 2026); level criteria set weekly by General Staff + Air Force with Cabinet, MoD, MVS, DSNS; all-clear siren repeat cancelled; Kyiv differentiated alerts from 6 Sep 2026 06:00; amendment No. 1128 in force 18 Sep 2026; No. 1129 sets railway operation by level (yellow: trains run; red: boarding and departures suspended). Euromaidan Press (4 Sep) states the business list and full criteria were not finalized and geographic targeting was not yet part of the system.
code_available: Not applicable. Official text on zakon.rada.gov.ua (in force, current version 18.09.2026); body not machine-retrievable on 2026-10-17 (HTTP 403 for print view).
takeaways_for_project: (1) Treat 2026-09-07 as a hard regime break; never mix pre- and post-reform data in one training set or metric (CLAUDE.md data rule; D-007/D-015). (2) The post-reform labelling rule is set weekly by the military and is unpublished, so the new regime is itself non-stationary (D-015 note); README must state any transfer result as a fact for that window only, with interpretations as hypotheses (D-015 amended). (3) Primary new-regime target = any level onset with any-level mask; red-only onset (red during yellow counts) as an extra row (D-015 (b), architecture item 4 target_levels). (4) Expect calibration-in-the-large failure of the frozen model a priori; this justifies the conditional README conclusion 'retraining/recalibration needed after the reform' (D-015 (d)). (5) Staggered rollout (Kyiv 6 Sep, pilots ~8 Sep) plus the 7-12 Sep data hole means the first post-reform days are unreliable; starting the API window at 2026-09-13 is justified. (6) Geographic narrowing would reduce share of time under alert without a change in threat; the before/after table (D-015 (a)) should be read with this caveat. (7) Any future yellow-regime model requires the human's explicit approval (Scope).
best_practices: Adopt: cite the primary act (No. 1092 + No. 1128) with dates when describing the regime break; record the rollout timeline in DECISIONS/README; keep the target-level and mask settings consistent; report post-reform results as exploratory with calibration-in-the-large; prefer adaptive baselines (rolling recent rate) as the bar in a drifting regime. Avoid: treating 'yellow' as equivalent to the pre-reform alert; using weekly-changing criteria as if fixed; claiming causal effects of the reform on attack intensity from alert counts (alert counts reflect declaration rules, not only threats); relying on unverified media statistics (e.g. 61/39 yellow/red share) in the report.
